meta.title: $\pi$ Shift Bragg Grating for Acousto Optic Sensing: Research Overview
meta.subtitle: Maximizing $Q$ at a fixed 20\,$\mu$m mode and $-3$\,dB insertion loss, November 2025 to September 2026
meta.author: Evyatar Rubin

frames.title: Only cavity local changes escape the loss versus width trade
items: \textbf{Goal:} a $\pi$ shift Bragg grating with a fixed \textbf{20\,$\mu$m} mode, maximizing $Q$ at \textbf{$-3$\,dB}. Materials are lossless, so every lever manages radiation.
\textbf{Teeth:} apodization, tooth shifts and tooth shapes all reduce loss \emph{and} widen the mode. Only cavity local changes, new scatterers and the lab's overshoot apodization escape.
\textbf{TE and TM} plain gratings tie at the operating point (13k). TM radiates in the propagation plane and responds to lateral structures (trench +35\,\%, circle rows +30\,\%); TE does not.

\textbf{Inverse design} (25 free teeth per side, width held fixed) is the largest measured gain: $Q = 88.9$k, 6.4$\times$ plain. Still below the lab's TE overshoot (projected $2$ to $3.4\times10^{5}$); in progress.
\textbf{Dead ends,} all measured: reflectors of every kind, in core hole lattices, BIC and Kerker scatterers, a second cavity, shaped trenches, exotic teeth.

frames.title: At 20\,$\mu$m and $-3$\,dB the inverse design leads by 6.4$\times$
frames.note: SiN 1.97 / SiO$_2$ 1.444, 350\,nm core, corrugation in nm, $\lambda \approx 1560$\,nm; each device lengthened until $T = 0.5$ at 20 $\pm$ 1\,$\mu$m, where $Q(-3\,\text{dB}) \approx 0.29\,Q_i$ is set by radiation alone. Overshoot rows are the lab's profile: TM interpolated to $T = 0.5$, TE projected from measured $Q_i$.

frames.title: Three tiers: lateral structures, inverse design, TE overshoot
frames.caption: Loaded $Q$ at the operating point. The two overshoot bars are the lab's profile, not ours: TM interpolated to $T = 0.5$, TE the midpoint of the projected $2.0$ to $3.4\times10^{5}$ range, never measured at $-3$\,dB.

frames.title: TE: apodization cuts loss most and widens the mode most
rows: 10 apodized periods per side: mode 15 to 20\,$\mu$m
5 $\approx$ 10; 20 to 40 add nothing; slight resonance shift
not a taper: overshoots to $\sim$2.4$\times$ bulk, dips, settles; $Q_i$ $\sim$15$\times$ ours in TE, 2.6$\times$ in TM
frames.note: Directions at equal period count. Apodization removes the abrupt envelope corner at the cavity, which radiates like an antenna; the far field drops one to two orders of magnitude with 10 apodized periods. The overshoot profile is the strongest lever on the table and we did not invent it.

frames.title: TE: the innermost tooth shift cuts loss at no width cost
rows: innermost pair shifted outward (100 to 140\,nm plateau)
loss down at no width cost; $Q$ rises modestly
most of a full apodization's $T$ at a much tighter mode
two teeth + cavity width, PSO (5 parameters)
gradient not needed; experiment confirms the shift range, $Q$ 1.3 to 1.5$\times$ simulation
ceiling $\Delta T \approx$ +0.001 to +0.006 beyond the shift
frames.note: The shift tunes the innermost reflection to the cavity round trip, $\mathrm{arg}(r) + k_0\, n_\text{eff}\, L_\text{cav} = 0$, redirecting light that would leak at the cavity corner into the mode. A $k$ space budget sets the ceiling: only $\sim$15\,\% of the radiated power originates within one tooth of the cavity.

frames.title: TE and TM tie at the operating point but radiate differently
rows: 3$\times$ weaker coupling: less lossy, lower $Q$, wider
$\sim$60\,\% in the propagation plane, sharp lobe 11 to 12$^\circ$ off axis
frames.note: The TM mode has half the TE margin in $k$ space to the cladding light line ($n_\text{eff} - n_\text{clad}$ smaller), so envelope changes radiate more easily; the 350 $\times$ 800\,nm core is past the aspect ratio where the TM bandgap weakens.

frames.title: TM: tooth level detuning always widens; narrowing is under 1\,\%
rows: no optimum; the loss lives in the arms
20 to 40\,\% worse than the lumped shift
+ see saw on the two inner teeth
fancier cavity shapes null or worse; mirror symmetry is optimal
frames.note: The envelope decays as $\exp(-\int q\,dx)$ with $q = \sqrt{\kappa^2 - \delta^2} \le \kappa$: any tooth level detuning $\delta$ can only lower $q$ and widen the mode. Narrowing needs $\kappa$ raised near the centre, which only cavity local changes or new scatterers can do; every measured narrowing is under 1\,\% (trench $-$0.9\,\%, circle row $-$0.4\,\%).

frames.title: TM: an air trench raises $Q$ by 35\,\% without widening the mode
text: A trench 1.8\,$\mu$m from the guide is the first lever that raises $T$ with the mode width unchanged or slightly narrower ($-$0.9\,\%): $Q$ \textbf{+35\,\%} (full depth) or \textbf{+22\,\%} (stopping at the core top, single lithography).

Total internal reflection at the oxide to air wall (lobe at $\sim$79$^\circ$, critical angle $\sim$44$^\circ$) shrinks the in plane light cone; a metal wall at the same place gives an equal loss, so it is the low index wall, not a mirror.
A straight wall is optimal; shaped trenches measured worse. TE null. The deep etch conflicts with the PDMS acoustic cover, which motivated the circles.

frames.title: TM: a SiN post row matches the trench in one lithography step
frames.caption: The post row ($r \approx 80$ to 110\,nm, 1.8\,$\mu$m from the guide) is a weak grating for the guided carrier and out couples a beam at $n_\text{clad}\sin\theta = n_\text{eff} - \lambda/\Lambda$; at the cutoff $\Lambda_c = \lambda/(n_\text{eff}+n_\text{clad}) \approx 531$\,nm it lands on the lobe, and sliding the row along $x$ sets the phase $\varphi = 360^\circ\,\delta x/\Lambda$. Left: $T$ follows a sinusoid in $\varphi$ (lobe $\times$2.2 at 90$^\circ$, $\times$0.45 at 270$^\circ$); at 0$^\circ$, where we started, the row hurts. Right: at 270$^\circ$ the period sweep peaks near 530\,nm; an air hole version flips the sign.

frames.title: TM: a second post row adds 3\,\%; rows are designed analytically
text: At the operating point: +16\,\% (57 posts, $r$ 80), +26\,\% (61 posts, $r$ 110), +30\,\% (pair at $\pm$12\,$\mu$m), on par with the full trench; width $-$0.4\,\%.

A row's cost is set by its two ends, its gain by the carrier it sees: the pair is nearly additive at $N = 80$ (figure) but only +3\,\% over one long row at the operating point; a third row adds nothing. Stacked rows, more rows in $y$, radius apodization: null or worse.
Circles do not stack with apodization, which already removes the lobe, but do stack with the inverse design. Freed there, they drifted under 1\,nm: their optimum is separable from the teeth.

frames.title: Inverse design: 25 free teeth per side at a fixed mode width
text: 3D adjoint optimization (lumopt2) on a 100 period per side TM surrogate. \textbf{191 parameters}: depth, width and shift of the 25 innermost teeth per side (mirrored), cavity width, and the circle row (frozen in practice).

Cost: peak transmission. Hard constraints: mode width inside a $\pm$2\,\% band and a fixed resonance; the gradient step is projected so it changes neither. $Q$ is never in the cost: at fixed width the loaded $Q$ is pinned, so every $T$ gain is a radiation $Q$ gain.
The optimized profile rises gently over the 25 free teeth (325 to $\sim$364\,nm), a mild version of the lab's overshoot.

frames.title: Inverse design: projecting on width and resonance works
rows: failed silently: true FWHM grew 15\,\% while $\sigma$ held
failed twice: width drifts to the band edge
failed: the resonance drifted and dragged the width
works: seed $T$ 0.90 to 0.964 (hand re trim) to 0.968 machine driven, resonance held, $Q_i$ 110k to 124k
\textbf{$Q$ = 88,868} at $N$ = 220, 6.4$\times$ plain TM (3 samples per linewidth)
paused: optimizer housekeeping bugs, not physics; fixes written, not yet redeployed
frames.note: Ranked next: restart; free 60 teeth instead of 25; free the circle row as a separate arm; a TE lane seeded from the overshoot profile, since TM $Q_i$ is capped near 150k to 250k by its light cone margin and the lab's TE $Q_i$ is 7 to 13$\times$ ours. The optimizer's mesher reads the width band as $\sim$18.3\,$\mu$m, $\sim$20\,$\mu$m in the standard mesher; never mix them.
